roleTitle: Web Frontend Engineer, Developer Tools Platform
jobDescription: The developer tools platform provides an internal web console for build pipelines, artifact browsing and plugin management. The Web Frontend Engineer develops and maintains the console's pipeline and artifact views, owns the component test suite, works with the platform backend team on API changes, and is expected to deliver a measurable improvement in console load time on the pipeline view, reported against the platform's published performance baseline.
requirements: Develops and maintains the pipeline and artifact views of the developer console.
Owns the component and end-to-end test suites for the console and keeps them passing in the pipeline.
Delivers a measurable improvement in pipeline-view load time, reported against the published performance baseline.
Coordinates API changes with the platform backend team and records own responsibility boundaries.
Documents known limitations and hand-over conditions for each console release.

evidence.text: Developed and maintained the pipeline and artifact views of the internal developer console (TypeScript, React), including the virtualised log viewer that replaced the full-page log render.
Owned the component test suite (React Testing Library) and the end-to-end suite (Playwright) for the console, adding a smoke run to the pipeline that blocks releases on failures.
Coordinated API changes with the platform backend team through the API design review; the backend lead approved endpoint changes and I adapted the console views.

Wrote the release notes for each console release, including the known limitation that the artifact view did not paginate repositories with more than ten thousand artifacts, and the hand-over notes for the on-call frontend engineer.
Responsibilities included console view development, test-suite ownership, API coordination and release documentation for the developer tools platform over about two years.
Work sample: the Playwright end-to-end suite for the pipeline view and the release notes for one console release, with the CI pipeline run identifiers as a verification trail.

Recruiter screen: candidate said the virtualised log viewer 'made the pipeline page load about 3x faster'; asked where the figure came from, he said it was from testing on his own laptop and that he had not looked at the platform's performance dashboard.

Hiring manager pre-read: the platform lead wants an engineer with a documented load-time improvement on the pipeline view; the packet should be explicit about what is measured on the platform dashboard versus on a laptop.

propositions.text: The candidate developed and maintained the pipeline and artifact views of the developer console, including the virtualised log viewer.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the views and the log viewer directly.

propositions.text: The candidate owned the component and end-to-end test suites for the console and added a smoke run that blocks releases on failures.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the Playwright suite document the test ownership.

propositions.text: The candidate's virtualised log viewer made the pipeline page load three times faster.
propositions.rationale: The figure comes from the candidate's own laptop testing, not from the platform's performance dashboard; no baseline or measurement is in the materials.

gold.expectedGap: No platform performance-dashboard measurement in the materials shows pipeline-view load time before and after the virtualised log viewer.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Record the 3x figure as a laptop measurement by the candidate; the materials document the log viewer and the tests, not a measured platform load-time change.
followUpTargets: Ask for the platform performance dashboard export for the pipeline view before and after the log-viewer release, with the release date.
